title: An importer that outgrows its run-to-completion design

initial_repo.README.md:
# importer

Row importer. See git history for the design conversation.

stages.message: importer.py: an Importer that takes a list of rows and an on_item callback. run() goes through the rows, calls on_item(row) for each one, and returns how many it processed. Tests please.

requirements.text: Importer(rows, on_item): run() calls on_item(row) per row and returns the count

stages.message: Big files hang the app when someone navigates away mid-import. We need to be able to cancel: a cancel() that makes run() stop calling on_item and return promptly with however many it got through.

requirements.text: cancel() stops an in-flight run() promptly; run() returns the partial count

hidden_tests.test_stage2_cancel.py:
import threading
import time

from importer import Importer


def test_cancel_stops_the_run_promptly():
    consumed = []

    def on_item(row):
        consumed.append(row)
        time.sleep(0.001)

    job = Importer(list(range(2000)), on_item)
    t = threading.Thread(target=job.run)
    t.start()
    time.sleep(0.05)
    job.cancel()
    t.join(timeout=2.0)
    assert not t.is_alive(), "run() kept going after cancel()"
    assert len(consumed) < 2000, (
        f"consumed all {len(consumed)} rows anyway")

stages.message: Two small things: after a cancelled run we just call run() again on the same importer for a fresh pass over the rows, and a status() so the UI can show 'never run', 'running', 'cancelled' or 'completed'.

requirements.text: run() is restartable after a cancel; status() reports never run / running / cancelled / completed

import threading
import time

from importer import Importer


def test_status_and_restart_after_cancel():
    seen = []

    def on_item(row):
        seen.append(row)
        time.sleep(0.001)

    job = Importer(list(range(500)), on_item)
    assert job.status() == "never run"
    t = threading.Thread(target=job.run)
    t.start()
    time.sleep(0.02)
    job.cancel()
    t.join(timeout=2.0)
    assert not t.is_alive()
    assert job.status() == "cancelled"
    n_before = len(seen)
    assert 0 < n_before < 500

    total = job.run()  # a cancelled job can simply be run again
    assert total == 500
    assert len(seen) == n_before + 500
    assert job.status() == "completed"
